reviews.title: Shockingly bad app!!
reviews.text:
This app feels obviously vibe coded. There’s no love in it, and it comes off like a cash grab. 

As for the words themselves, they’re always presented as real words, but are sometimes exceedingly obscure (like it was used once in a Shakespeare play and never again in human language) or they’re from another language and are passed off as English. 

Anytime a word comes up that seems interesting I have to fact check it myself to make sure that:
A) this really is a word used in English, and
B) the definition is what the app claims it to be.

VERY OFTEN the short definition provided by the app is misleading or inadequate. 


Does the app still provide some use and value? Yes. 

Do I feel upset that this is what counts for quality? Yes.

reviews.title: Why is there no one a day widget option?
reviews.text: I really like the concept of this app, but I’m baffled by one particular design decision. The Lock Screen widget offers refresh options for Never, Twice a Day, Occasionally, Frequently, and Very Frequently, yet somehow there’s no option for once a day. For an app designed to help people expand their vocabulary, this seems like an incredibly obvious omission. I want to learn one new word each day and have it remain on my Home Screen long enough to actually retain it. Constantly cycling through new words defeats that purpose. Even the slowest refresh option introduces 1–2 words per day. A simple once-daily refresh setting would make this app significantly more useful for people who prioritize learning and retention over sheer exposure to new words.

reviews.title: Wrong definitions
reviews.text:
I tested 20 words and there have been many i didn’t find very accurate

Goad - it’s not “to urge”, it was over simplified the tone of the word

Sonsie - “Having a pleasing, curvy body” it’s not “curvy body” it’s attractive healthy body, also there are many other meanings like “happy” or “good fortune”

retrocedence - “The act of going back or returning” although not wrong, it’s oversimplified on how it’s actually used

sapiential - “Showing great wisdom or knowledge” this is fine, however the main usage of this word is about objects, which none of the example showed “relating to, derived from, or possessing wisdom.” Is better

pliancy - “Being able to adapt easily” It can describe a physical object that bends without breaking, or a person’s strong mind. It’s not like adapting because a lot of people (myself included) will think “mahoraga” and it’s not exactly right

esurient - “Hungry, greedy, or eager for something” it’s good, but it’s a stronger word than just hungry, it’s like starving for more

Befog - “To make someone feel confused.” It’s more like to make something unclear, confuse the mind, or cover in a physical fog. 


And this is just in the 20 i was testing. Often they’re undersimplfied, which i get but often misleading or just not the full definition

reviews.title: They don’t really care, as long as they get your money.
reviews.text:
Edited: The the premium version isn’t worth $50 a year. And any good opinion I had of the app is overshadowed by the horrible customer service. The developer’s FAQ site that’s linked in the App Store isn’t helpful to me as it doesn’t have any email contact information. So I’m leaving a review here. I’d like to cancel my subscription (I thought I had already done so but it seems in my haste all I did was cancel it after the first year). But I actually haven’t paid for it yet— it’s just pending on my account waiting for me to add a new payment method. I don’t not want this app. I don’t want to be charged for it at all. I deleted it off my phone. Your assistance would be greatly appreciated.

Edit: The developer responded to my review telling me to email them. That they would help me. But I still have heard NOTHING after sending 2 emails. (Not even an automated message) Just know, that if you’re in the same position, they may not actually get back to you in a timely manner. If at all. Seems to me they *just want the money* and don’t actually care about providing good customer service. I hope I’m wrong. Will keep you posted.

Update: I’ve heard nothing back after more than two weeks. 😪

reviews.title: A misleading waste of time

If you’re going to entice people to take an assessment of their current ability, which requires an investment of their time, and you’re going to lock the results  behind a subscription, then it is beyond disrespectful of people’s time to spring the subscription requirement on them only after they’ve invested their time completing the assessment! That is a fundamentally manipulative sales technique that relies on people’s reluctance to have wasted time that they’ve already spent. It’s a shameful approach to selling subscription to what might actually be a nice app. I was actually considering subscribing before that experience, but now it would just feel dirty.

reviews.title: Can’t check if the app works for me
reviews.text: Don’t want to subscribe straight away and also there is no monthly payment. What if I don’t like the app. Wasted my time

reviews.title: Potential, but the app is poor
reviews.text:
I wanted to love this app. It seems well-designed at first glance but further use found several glitches.

First, the pronunciations are not always accurate. I came across the word Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious, which is well known from the Mary Poppins song. When I clicked the audio, it was pronounced incorrectly. If such a well-known word is pronounced wrongly, how can you trust that others aren’t as well?

Next, after I had added about 18 words to my collection of words I want to learn, they suddenly were no longer accessible and a new collection started. Today, that second collection had also disappeared and it started a new one again. None of my words are there anymore.

Finally, when I went to cancel my free trial, it offered me a special discount (50% off). When I clicked the offer, it sent me to a page to redeem it, where it promptly told me I was not eligible for the offer and would not process it. Makes no sense.

An app this expensive can’t afford to be this glitchy. It might be worth $10 a year with the current functionality but definitely not $50 or $60.

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text: Very dodgy app, I was charged 47.99 for no reason even after cancelling. No subscriptions are 47.99 so I don’t have a clue where this has come from. Please never download you will subjected to random charges at any time. Also uses wrong spellings. All together an awful app I’d stay far clear from. Been over two weeks and you’re still ignoring all emails. Why dos apple let these horrible dodgy people even make scams like this, they should be held responsible.

reviews.title: Not the best first impression - free trial sign up required at the end of a so called free test
reviews.text: First day and I’m annoyed by it already. My time is very valuable and I don’t get much free time so I was annoyed to be tricked into taking a free vocabulary test, spending time checking what words I know, only to be taken to the end where it forces you to sign up for a free trial in order to view your results. You can’t see your results unless you take out the free trial. Yeah I can do the free trial but I know apps like this rely on people to take out the free trial then forget they took it out then get charged for it. But annoyed it said free test and then to view your results after taking time to do the test your only option is to sign up for the trial. That’s just wrong and unfair. So right now it’s a 1 star from me. I’m not happy. I’m going to go back into the app and keep using it. If things improve or I get a better experience I’ll come back and change my review accordingly, but not the best first impression. Also when it gave me the option to add a widget to my Home Screen all it did was open my Home Screen then it did nothing else. So I just opened up the app again and it opened to the home page of the app. So much for the widget.

reviews.title: Shoves premium in your face too much
reviews.text: The general idea of the app is good and I’m enjoying learning words but premium is pushed on you at every opportunity. Normally id be fine with this as the app is good at what it does. But it actually deliberately wastes your time. An option pops up asking if I want to do a vocabulary quiz for free to see my vocab level. I spend 10 mins and do the quiz only to be told at the end I need to pay to see the results. Waste of time and made me uninstall the app

reviews.title: Not free!!!
reviews.text: Ridiculous - I spent ages setting up the app and then it says “start 3 days free trial”.

reviews.title: Rubbish
reviews.text: Half the words I found were wrong. I went to a dictionary to double check and everything had different meanings. You need to fix this immediately and stop making people pay to waste time

reviews.title: Predatory sales pitching
reviews.text: The way they advertised it as a few pounds a month was misleading I signed up expecting to be able to stop after a month or two but then I saw I was on a year package. The wording of it was very misleading and now I’m down £35 for the whole year when I only wanted a month or so. Very disappointing

reviews.title: Bad
reviews.text: First of all I pressed on the free trial button and instantly was charged with 23 bucks. Secondly, I don’t want to sound rude, your design looks fancy but the product itself is bull***t. I live in the US but I’m not native and I wanted to enrich my vocabulary with words I can use if not everyday at least sometimes. If I say these words to my American comrades they would think that I got sick. I am very “parsimonious” regarding this app. My advice is to apply ai in your app to evaluate the level of a user and give suitable words. You asked to choose which words I know and the list was supposed to be “intermediate” but that was some “William Shakespeare” English words list. If you apply these suggestions I would give you a better review now I don’t see any reason to do that. Thank you for your attention and thank you in advance for consideration.!

reviews.title: I tried
reviews.text: I tried to use it. And I understand they make the money from the subscriptions. But I wanted to use the free version for a while first, to get a feel for it. But I just got spammed over and over by going premium I gave up. Notifications. Pop ups in the app. Every time. Over and over. No turn off like the stink of desperation.

reviews.title: Yet another simple app that charges you a monthly subscription
reviews.text: Most users would happily watch a 30 second ad once every time they use an app rather than pay a monthly subscription

reviews.title: Needs heavy improvement
reviews.text: I was getting way too many notifications, multiple per hour after setting up vocab for less than one per hour. When I went in to the app, twice, I could not find how to change the frequency of how often you get notifications. That should be extraordinarily clear for user experience purposes. I went in and could change the basic level of words I receive with no guidance on what sorts of words I’d see, but no frequency of notification changes in the setting menu. I’ve decided to uninstall the app after being frustrated and not being able to change the experience. It’s a decent concept, I like learning new words, but this has a very poor user experience right now. I’d recommend you wait until this issue is fixed so you aren’t spammed with notifications like I was, it was so annoying.

reviews.title: Charges after 3 days.
reviews.text: Seems as though loads of front loaded questions only to be asked ‘try 3 days for free’ and only one option to continue. So seems like it’s only free for 3 days then costs money. Shame.
